newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey coalition allies to meet amid polls talk.
newsitem.headline: Turkey coalition allies to meet amid polls talk.

text.p: Turkish Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan was to meet his coalition partner Tansu Ciller on Friday in bargaining over possible early elections to solve a government crisis over Islamist activism.
"They will meet today but the time has not been fixed yet," an aide to conservative Foreign Minister Ciller told Reuters.
Ciller said on Thursday she would press Erbakan, modern Turkey's first Islamist leader, to make her prime minister in a caretaker government that would take the country to the polls.
Elections would normally be due by the year 2000.

The 11-month-old alliance between Erbakan and pro-Western Ciller has been crumbling under pressure from the secularist establishment, which sees Erbakan's Welfare Party as the source of an Islamist revival in officially secular Turkey.

The pair are set to swop jobs next year under a power-sharing deal that established their alliance last June. But Ciller says she can ward off anti-Islamist pressure on the government from the army if she takes the top job sooner.
The Turkish press said on Friday that Erbakan had agreed to hand over power to Ciller but that the pair disagreed on when new elections should take place.
The Hurriyet daily said Erbakan, whose party is facing closure in an anti-Islamist crackdown, wants to go to the nation in October while Ciller favours next March.
